page_title: Tracking toil with SRE principles | Google Cloud Blog

sources.entry: Identifying and tracking toil using SRE principles

summary.name: Tracking toil with SRE principles
summary.one_liner: A Google Cloud blog post explaining how SRE teams identify, measure, and eliminate "toil" (manual, repetitive, automatable operational work) using Google SRE principles.
use_cases: Deciding which manual operational tasks to automate first
Measuring how much team time goes to interrupts and manual requests
Running a quarterly team survey on toil
Setting a toil budget (e.g., under 50% of time)
Distinguishing operational toil from valuable system complexity
summary.what_it_does: The post defines toil using the Google SRE book's definition and gives examples such as handling quota requests, applying schema changes, and copying commands from playbooks. It describes identifying toil by logging requests as tickets with lightweight metadata (work type, difficulty, who did it) and by running periodic team surveys. It recommends measuring toil monthly or quarterly and keeping it under 50% of each SRE's time. For elimination, it suggests automation, treating automation as production code, using the ticketing system as a self-service API, and limiting toil work to assigned people such as an on-call rotation. It also distinguishes toil from complexity, which it frames as a user-experience problem.
notable: Defines toil using the Google SRE book's chapter 5 definition
Includes a sample toil survey with questions teams can reuse
Recommends keeping toil below 50% of SRE time
caveats: Describes Google's internal practices; it is not a product or tool with setup steps
Tracking metadata and survey guidance are lightweight suggestions, not a prescribed system
